data.name: Stevie
data.gender_notes: Stevie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Given name Stevie is derived from the name Stewart which is composed of two Old English words ‘stig’ and ‘weard’ meaning ‘crown’ and ‘guardian’ or ‘steward’ respectively. The name Stevie is used as a diminutive or a nickname for the name Stewart and can be used for both boys and girls. The name Stevie carries the meaning “Crown” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Stevie usually hope their child will grow to embody crown and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Stevie is a name that carries a deep spiritual meaning, it is a reminder to be a crown bearer, a guardian, and a steward of your life. It is a name that symbolizes leadership, responsibility, and protection. It is also a name that resonates with the energy of music, creativity, and rebellion.
data.etymology: Stevie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Crown.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Stevie total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_greek.name: Στίβι
in_greek.meaning: Παράγωγο του Στεφανός, που σημαίνει στεφάνι ή κορόι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Στίβι είναι μια σύντομη μορφή του ονόματος Στεφανός, το οποίο προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει στεφάνι ή κορόι. Ο Στεφανός αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη ως ο πρώτος μάρτυρας των Χριστιανών, ο Άγιος Στεφανός. Το όνομα είναι συμβολικό για τη νίκη και την επιτυχία, και έχει μεγάλη σημασία στο Χριστιανισμό.

data.cultural_impact: Stevie, as a diminutive from the name Stewart, has long held a significant impact in popular culture across music, sports, and entertainment industries. One of the most celebrated figures bearing the moniker was the legendary rock musician Stevie Ray Vaughan. His electrifying guitar work helped to revive the blues and brought new life to the guitar genre. Another gifted individual was Stevie Wonder, a blind musician who soared to the heights of Motown with his critical and commercial successes. Stevie Nicks, a Grammy Award-winning singer-songwriter and a member of the iconic band Fleetwood Mac, has also contributed to the cultural legacy of the name with her enchanting voice and spellbinding stage presence.

It represents the gentle, caring, and thoughtful nature of serving and nurturing all aspects of our existence. The spiritual significance of the name can be seen in the lives of significant Stevies throughout history and contemporary life who have embraced their stewardship and let their light shine brightly to inspire, comfort, and uplift others. Stevie is a reminder that each of us has a purpose and a role to play in the grand tapestry of creation, and that by graciously accepting the trust and responsibility bestowed upon us, we can fulfill our potential and bring honor and sanctity to our lives.

historical_references.reference: Stephen of Thessalonica, also known as Stephanos or Stephanos of Thessalonica, was a Greek saint and martyr who lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. He was the Bishop of Thessalonica during the time when Emperor Maximian persecuted Christians. According to legend, Stephanos was subjected to various forms of torture, including being sawn in half with a saw. He is venerated as a patron saint of deacons and horses.

Stevie Wonder is an American musician, singer-songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist. Born Stevland Hardaway Judkins on May 13, 1941, he was given the name 'Little Stevie Wonder' as a child due to his exceptional musical talent. He began performing in public at a young age and signed his first record contract at the age of 13. Stevie's Christian name was likely given to him in reference to Stephen of Thessalonica, the early Christian martyr and patron saint of deacons.
